Subject: SLO appeal: tail-latency spike during checkout window

Hi Chloe,

We're raising an SLO appeal for FastTrack Payments. On 2028-07-07 between ~23:43 and 00:18 UTC we observed a significant tail-latency spike on Redwood endpoints used by our checkout flow (tokenization and authorize calls). Our customer-facing telemetry shows an increase in 503s and checkout timeouts; we estimate ~0.7% of transactions retried or failed during the window which materially impacted revenue.

We need Redwood to:
- Confirm the service-side request/availability window you see for our account (FastTrack)
- Provide the raw trace bundle and SRE analysis that will support an SLO credit claim if eligible
- Share next steps and a timeline for a post-incident writeup and remediation plan

I've attached client-side traces (client_traces_fasttrack_20280707.zip) and a short CSV with observed failed transaction IDs. Please advise who we should loop in on the Redwood side; happy to schedule a short call.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Ops Lead, FastTrack Payments

Chloe / team — preliminary findings from the 23:40-00:20 UTC window:
- We see increased queue depth on three shards in us-west-2 starting 23:42:11 UTC; the scheduler triggered a short-lived eviction at ~23:43:05 UTC while a model quantization job completed on the node.
- KV cache misses spiked for a subset of heavy tokenization requests which amplified p99 latency. Network and LB health checks show no region-wide outage.
- I attached an excerpt (infra-trace-excerpt.txt) with the scheduler logs and aligned request IDs that map to FastTrack's client traces.

Assessment: this looks like a localized capacity preemption + cache-warm effect rather than a global control-plane outage. That said, the customer-facing impact is real. Based on the SLA language, we have an availability delta during 23:42:11 - 23:50:30 UTC that could be eligible for proportional remedy.

Next steps:
- I'll produce the full trace bundle and place it in SUP-1234 for review.
- Aditya, we'll need your run at prorated credit; I'm estimating ~8-12 minutes of affected per-shard degraded window but final numbers depend on request alignment.

Diego

Hi Lisa — thanks for your patience. Update and proposed remedy below.

Summary of confirmed window: 2028-07-07 23:42:11 - 23:50:30 UTC (server-side aligned). Evidence: scheduler eviction logs, LB request alignment, and KV-miss amplification (see attached infra-trace-excerpt.txt).

Eligibility: Per our SLO wording and the proportional remediation clause, FastTrack appears eligible for a prorated credit for the affected minutes where availability dropped below the agreed threshold. Aditya has attached a draft calculation (redwood_slo_calc_20280708.xlsx) showing the prorated credit based on token consumption and impacted p99 latency buckets.

Recommended next steps:
- We will route a credit for the prorated interval shown in the spreadsheet; please confirm the billing account and preferred invoice adjustment (credit vs. invoice reduction).
- We will schedule a short postmortem with SRE and Platform PMs next week; proposed time: Thu 2028-07-12 10:00 PT. Invite: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234
- Long-term remediation: SRE will add a guard to avoid scheduler-triggered model reloads during heavy checkout windows and increase KV cache warmup prioritization for tokenization routes.

If you confirm the billing details we will process the credit and share the full postmortem notes after the scheduled review.

Apologies for the impact — we take these seriously and will follow up with mitigation work.

Regards,
